title: Tenant Residency-aware Access Evidence Exporter
creator: Michael Chen
description: Background: Enterprise customers in regulated regions require exports of access evidence scoped to data residency boundaries and retention policies. Current exports are tenant-global and lack per-residency filtering, causing manual work for compliance teams and delaying audits. Problem: We need a reproducible, auditable evidence exporter that combines RBAC state, SSO/SAML session records, SCIM provisioning events, and periodic access-review snapshots, filtered by tenant residency and retention windows. Goal: Build a residency-aware access evidence exporter service and a lightweight orchestration runbook that can produce signed, time-bounded reports per tenant-region. The exporter should integrate with the existing evidence pipeline, support both on-demand and scheduled exports, and ensure minimal outage risk during rollout.
design_notes:
- Data model: export proto rows with fields: tenant_id, residency_region, export_window_start, export_window_end, user_id, role_assignments, scim_events (provision/deprovision), sso_sessions (start/end, idp), access_review_snapshot_id, signing_hash. Keep rows denormalized for downstream auditors.
- Filtering: residency resolved from tenant metadata (tenant.residency or tenant.primary_region). If tenant has multi-region residency, apply per-tenant retention map.
- RBAC source: materialized role-assignment view updated every 5m. SCIM/source-of-truth events pulled from the scim-change-stream topic. SSO/SAML sessions pulled from session-store with retention-aware windowing.
- Export orchestration: a Kubernetes job per export request with ephemeral credentials to read required stores and write to encrypted objectstore (s3-compatible) with server-side encryption. Each export produces a signed manifest (ed25519) stored alongside the object.
- Privacy: PII redaction configurable per-tenant policy. Default: redact email domains for EU-residency tenants unless approval flag is true.
proposed_solution: Phase 1 (MVP): residency-aware on-demand exporter that accepts tenant_id + date-range + export-type (full-access|scim-only|session-only). Produces gzipped ndjson in s3://redwood-evidence/<tenant>/residency=<region>/<export-id>. Phase 2: scheduled exports (weekly/monthly), retention-aware purging, and integration into audit console with download TTL links. Phase 3: cross-tenant aggregated reports for internal compliance monitoring.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch with new service and small infra changes; unit/integration tests + e2e against staging. 2) Canary: enable for internal compliance tenant and 2 small customers (opt-in) for 2 weeks. 3) Full rollout behind feature flag with audit-logs enabled. 4) Post-rollout runbook and operator training.
acceptance_criteria: - Export produces region-filtered artifacts that contain only events within requested window and residency region. - Signed manifest verifiable by compliance team tool. - Default PII redaction applies for EU-residency tenants. - Export job resource usage stays within 0.5x of baseline (no noisy neighbor regressions). - End-to-end tests covering RBAC+SCIM+SSO integration pass in CI.
metrics: - Time-to-first-byte for export job (target < 30s for small tenant < 1k users). - Time-to-completion for full export (target < 20m for tenants < 100k events). - Number of exports per tenant per month. - Failed exports rate (target < 1%). - Audit-verified signature failures (target 0).
risks_and_mitigation: - Privacy risk if residency resolution wrong: add repeated residency validation step and manual override flow in console. - Performance risk pulling full session-store: use time-windowed reads and backpressure via Kafka consumer group. - Security risk for export artifacts access: require pre-signed URLs with short TTL and tenant-scoped ACLs. - Compliance/legal risk for retention mismatch: provide explicit mapping table between tenant retention policy and exporter retention parameters.

qa_and_tests: - Unit tests for residency resolution logic and PII redaction. - Integration tests: materialized RBAC view + scim-change-stream replay + session-store sample. - E2E test: create tenant with EU residency, provision users via SCIM, run export, verify redaction and signature. - Load test: synthetic 1M events export smoke test in perf cluster.
comments: 2026-02-21: Kickoff meeting notes added. PM and Legal clarified regulatory requirements for EU and APAC: signed manifests are required for auditability.
2026-02-26: Engineering design review — decided to use ed25519 for signatures to keep artifacts small and verification cheap. Reviewers: Priya Rao, Tomas Müller.
2026-03-02: Backend PR opened (WIP). Initial schema and job controller implemented. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4872
2026-03-05: Security review request submitted. Raised concern about ephemeral creds for job pods; plan to use short-lived KMS-backed tokens via identity service.
2026-03-09: QA reported intermittent failure when SCIM event backlog > 200k events; mitigation: incremental checkpointing + batch windowing. Assigned to Miguel Ortega for optimization.
2026-03-10: Blocker cleared — scim-change-stream consumer now supports range reads and resume tokens. Moving to canary for internal tenant.
Post-launch follow-ups: collect customer feedback loop for retention mapping UI in Console and add export telemetry to billing metrics (for audit cost attribution).
